0.1.n: Links Hamumu to the plushie, identifying which character it represents.

0.2.n: A noun for a stuffed toy, here one depicting Hamumu.

0.3.n: Politely finishes the statement; the subject is understood from context.

1.0.n: Used alone as an excited reaction.

1.2.n: With な, expresses admiration and a wish to have something similar.

1.3.n: Adds a wistful feeling to いい, suggesting friendly envy.

1.6.n: Connects the character’s name to the toy depicting it.

1.7.n: The speaker repeats this noun phrase as the object of their admiration.

2.0.n: Introduces something the listener may not yet know.

2.1.n: The speaker refers to themself; も follows to include them alongside someone else.

2.2.n: Marks 私 as another person who shares this enthusiasm.

2.3.n: This is the first part of the title ハムスターアイドル烈伝, not a separate animal being discussed.

2.4.n: Part of the title; アイドル refers to a pop entertainer or celebrity.

2.5.n: 烈伝 is the final part of the title, giving it a grand, heroic tone.

2.6.n: Expresses strong liking; casual speech leaves out が after the title here.

2.7.n: The linking form of だ follows 大好き and leaves the thought open for what comes next.

3.0.n: This is the character’s name; the topic particle は is omitted in casual speech.

3.1.n: 可愛い describes the character, and です makes the statement polite.

3.2.n: Adds emphasis to the speaker’s opinion before ね invites agreement.

3.3.n: Invites the listener to agree with the speaker’s enthusiasm.

0.tip: Name + の + ぬいぐるみ means a plushie depicting that character, not necessarily a toy they own.

1.tip: いいな often expresses friendly envy: the speaker thinks something is nice and wishes they had it too.

2.lit: Actually, I too, Hamster Idol Heroic Biographies, really like, and…
2.tip: Ending with で links 大好き to the next thought instead of finishing the sentence.

3.lit: Hamumu is cute, you know, right!
3.tip: よね combines an enthusiastic statement with an invitation for the listener to agree.
